newsitem.title: USA: Ralston says he has learned from mistakes.
newsitem.headline: Ralston says he has learned from mistakes.

text.p: Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston said on Thursday he had worked "to learn from my mistakes" and thanked Defence Secretary William Cohen for supporting his candidacy to become chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff despite a previous adulterous affair.
Ralston, vice chairman of the joint chiefs, gave no indication in a brief statement released at the Pentagon that he might withdraw his candidacy for the nation's top military job.
"I take full responsibility for my conduct some years ago and have worked diligently to learn from my mistakes," said Ralston, who is travelling in Kazakhstan and other former Soviet states.
"Our armed forces are composed of human beings that strive to meet the highest standards every day, but I am acutely aware of human strengths and human frailties," he said.

The White House and Pentagon said on Thursday that Ralston remained a leading candidate to become chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff despite news this week that he had an adulterous affair 13 years ago while he was separated from his first wife. They were later divorced.

"I would like to express my deep appreciation for the understanding and support accorded me by Secretary of Defence Cohen, General Shalikashvili (Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Gen. John Shalikashvili), my family and numerous others from within and outside the military in these recent days," Ralston said.
